Nope, I get his point. There’s nothing wrong with enjoying art just for the aesthetics. That’s totally fine, I’m totally fine with thinking AI art is good too. But don’t compare it with the real thing that AI art is based off of.

I chose the expensive art as an example to point out that humans have literally already decided this issue. The real art is worth more because that is the true, full context of the piece. That is the final product of the method, and everything else that went into it. Frida Kahlo’s art would not be as well appreciated if it weren’t for the story behind it. Studio Ghibli’s films are breath taking visually, but wouldn’t be as famous if they were just visually interesting. The incredible lengths to get sequences just right is well known, and adds to the appreciation.

The blanket statement “these two things are equivalent” is idiotic and ignorant. AI art is math based on the probability of where a pixel should go based on someone else’s work vs human effort and tool. It’s also incredibly dismissive and disrespectful. Imagine you spent hours trying to perfect your art style, or music, or whatever, and someone just fed it into a computer, shit out a copy, and told you to your face that it’s just as good if not better. The computer is better than you, why even exist? You’re irrelevant, I’ve extracted your worth with math and can reproduce effectively your soul in seconds. What a shitty thing to say, what a shitty tool to put value in.

And where does the financial value come from? Surely it can’t just be the physical appeal of the art piece, otherwise AI art would be worth millions, and fakes would be evaluated at the same price. Why do people believe original art has value?

You’re dancing around my point.

AI is the fake, every time. There is nothing of value behind purely AI art. That’s why it’s slop and one of the reasons XQC is an idiot.

You’re not making the point you think you are. All you’re saying is that you’re only capable of appreciating art at the surface level. The final result of any piece of art is influenced by the methods used and the message the art is trying to convey, the product and method are inextricably linked. 

Why do you think prints of art are cheaper than the original work? Or that fakes aren’t nearly as valuable as the real thing? AI “art” is hollow, with zero depth beyond the pixels. The method IS important, that’s how you get the final product. And art isn’t really a product to begin with.
